subject: StellarGrid committed capacity: throughput fit & burst buffer proposal
messages:
From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@stellargrid.ai>

Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@stellargrid.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Initial capacity ask - sustained throughput targets & SLOs

Jonas —

Thanks for taking this. We're sizing committed capacity for StellarGrid's inference pipeline for our chat + summarization product. High-level workload: 8k active users (peak), average prompt + context ~1,200 tokens, median response ~300 tokens. Expected peak concurrent requests: ~55. Target SLOs: p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 500ms for short responses (<=512 tokens) and <= 1.2s for long (>=1500 tokens).

We want Redwood Dedicated capacity committed for predictable unit economics and region affinity (us-west). Key asks for your sizing proposal:
- Recommended tokens/sec capacity to provision (sustained & burst)
- GPUs required for committed slab and recommended burst lanes
- Suggested safety buffer / headroom multiplier for peak events
- Fallback model variants and graceful degradation plan

Attached is a rough SLO matrix and our monthly token forecast (stellargrid_request.xlsx). Procurement is asking for a ballpark by EOD Wednesday so they can start internal approvals.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Kim
Head of ML Engineering, StellarGrid

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask - sustained throughput targets & SLOs

Sarah — thanks for the detail and the attachment. Quick read; below is an initial sizing sketch (ballpark) so procurement has numbers to work with. We'll iterate once Ben and Priyom run the commit economics.

Assumptions I used (please confirm):
- Primary model: open-70b-quant (q4f16) with typical generation profile: avg 300 tokens per response at 50% prompt length; per-GPU steady tokens/sec = ~500 at seq=1024 on A100-class instance (conservative).
- Peak sustained tokens/sec target (derived from your peak concurrent 55 * avg 1500 tokens per full roundtrip / average response duration ~4s) => ~20,600 tokens/sec sustained peak.
- We include 25% operational headroom for autoscaling smoothing + cache warmup.

Sizing math (rounded):
- Baseline GPUs = ceil(20,600 / 500) = 42 GPUs
- With 25% headroom => 42 * 1.25 = 52.5 => recommend 53 GPUs committed (regional slab)
- Add 10% burst lanes (on-demand reserved burst or dedicated burst pool) = +6 GPUs for short spikes

Notes / tradeoffs:
- If you can accept a slightly higher latency p95 for long generations or move long-tail work to an async queue, we can drop committed GPUs by ~15-20% via burst-first strategy.
- Quantization to q8_0 (higher risk) or using an efficient 33B variant reduces per-request latency and could drop GPUs to ~35 committed. Ben: can you run a quick throughput delta for q8 vs q4f16?

Next steps: Ben and Priyom to produce two numbered proposal variants (conservative commit with low cost-sensitivity and lean commit + burst). I'll book a 30-min sync after that.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Quick follow-up with alternate mapping and a cost-saving option. I ran a microbench (seq=1024) with two stacks:
- Stack A: open-70b-quant (q4f16) -> ~500 tokens/sec/GPU (matches Jonas)
- Stack B: open-33b-adv (int8-ish) -> ~820 tokens/sec/GPU with slightly higher sampling variance on tail latency (p95 + ~90ms)

Option 1 - Conservative (matches Jonas): commit 53 GPUs (A100 equivalent), 10% burst lanes, headroom 1.25. Rationale: matches latency SLOs without changing model family.
Option 2 - Lean + Burst: commit 34 GPUs using Stack B primary (33B quant) for steady traffic + 12 burst GPUs on higher-performance instances for peak. Estimated committed cost = ~ -22% vs Option 1. Tail risk: p95 for long sequences may hit ~1.5s unless you route long generations to async.

Operational playbook (recommended):
- Canary deploy with 10% traffic on Stack B for 2 weeks and validate quality/regression evals (use Redwood Optimize eval set).
- Implement model routing policy by route: short-chat (<=512 tokens) -> 33B variant; long-form -> 70B q4f16 on committed pool, or queue-based fallthrough.

I attached a small workbook with per-GPU throughput deltas (commit_proposal_v1.xlsx).

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sarah — attaching the one-pager and a concise runbook link (Drive) with the proposed routing policy and fallback rules. High-level answers below:

Summary (one-pager highlights):- Option 1 (Conservative): 53 committed GPUs (A100-equivalent), 6 burst GPUs, estimated monthly token capacity ~4.7B tokens, estimated monthly cost range $210k–$260k depending on instance class/burst hours.- Option 2 (Lean + Burst): 34 committed GPUs (33B primary), 12 burst GPUs, estimated monthly token capacity ~3.2B tokens steady + bursts, estimated monthly cost range $165k–$195k.

Region & Security: both options can be provisioned in us-west with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. We'll include those as contract terms; Rafael will attach the SOC2 excerpts for procurement.

Fallback & Graceful Degrade:
- Primary: automatic model routing (short -> 33B, long -> 70B) with timeout thresholds.
- If burst lanes exhausted: respond with 503 + Retry-After when request is latency-sensitive; for background long-form jobs we enqueue and return structured job id.
- Canary: 10% traffic shift for 14 days, continuous quality monitor; Redwood Optimize alerts on any generation regressions against the eval set.

Action items and timeline:
1) Ben & Priyom: finalize line-item cost worksheet and per-GPU throughput table (EOD today).
2) Rafael: attach SOC2 and KMS integration appendix (today).
3) Jonas: prepare DocuSign template and the two-option one-pager (ready for signature in 48h once legal terms align).
